capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the first part, unfold the meaning of `Filter.smallSets (𝓝 x)`: it suffices to show that for every neighborhood `U` of `x`, sufficiently small radii `r → 0` satisfy
\[
\operatorname{closedBall}(x,r)\subseteq U.
\]
Choose `δ > 0` with `ball x δ ⊆ U`, using the pseudometric neighborhood basis. Eventually `r < δ`; then every point of `closedBall x r` has distance at most `r`, hence lies in `ball x δ`. Negative radii cause no issue because the corresponding closed ball is empty.

For the second part, represent
\[
\operatorname{sphere}(x,\varepsilon)=\{y\mid \operatorname{dist}(y,x)=\varepsilon\}
\]
as the preimage of the closed singleton `{ε}` under the continuous function `y ↦ dist y x`. Thus the sphere is closed. These two standard pseudometric-space mechanisms should also correspond closely to existing `Metric` lemmas in Mathlib.
